solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Advocate scrubbing up exhibit

indicators.note: scrubbing means cancelling, so the word up is struck out of the longer word

parts.note: to advocate a cause is to support it

explanation.surface: A barrister cleans up a piece of evidence before presenting it in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Advocate' looks like the lawyer, but it is the verb; 'scrubbing' takes UP out of SUPPORT.
explanation.definitionFit: To sport something is to wear or show it off, so it means to exhibit.

clue.text: Hut holding old toilet art student originally exhibited

indicators.note: holding says the hut goes round the other pieces

parts.note: a shed is a hut
WC, water closet, is a toilet

indicators.note: originally takes the opening letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A student's early artwork was displayed in a shack housing an old lavatory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' gives A and S, the first letters of 'art' and 'student'.
explanation.definitionFit: To showcase something is to display it to advantage, so exhibited is a synonym.

clue.text: Offer up period dramas here

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a restaurant may do, or offer, a set lunch
an eon is a vast period of time

explanation.surface: An instruction to present costume dramas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns DO into OD.
explanation.definitionFit: An odeon is a cinema, or an ancient theatre, a place where dramas play.

clue.text: Young European with a bit up top

indicators.note: up top in a down clue says this piece goes above the other

parts.note: a tad is a bit
a Pole is a European

explanation.surface: A young continental with a little something on their head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Young' is a noun, the offspring of an animal, as tadpoles are of frogs.
explanation.definitionFit: A tadpole is a frog or toad's larva, an example of animal young.

clue.text: Protestant female new, replacing prison's first head of religion

indicators.note: replacing says one letter of the prison is swapped out for another

parts.note: Parkhurst is a prison on the Isle of Wight

indicators.note: the head of religion is its opening letter, and first says it is the earlier of the prison's two such letters that goes

explanation.surface: A religious form records a woman's details, with a new entry taking the place of the prison chaplain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Protestant' is not a church here but one who protests: Emmeline Pankhurst led the British suffragettes. N replaces the first R in PARKHURST.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmeline Pankhurst was a leading suffragette, a woman famous for protest.

clue.text: Incisive one in local Welsh town

indicators.note: in puts the numeral inside the town

parts.note: Ponty is the local name for Pontypridd in south Wales
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A sharp-witted resident of a small town in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: Pontypridd, a south Wales town, is known locally as Ponty.
explanation.definitionFit: Pointy remarks are sharp and to the point, so incisive.

clue.text: One with eye on boat as luxury

indicators.note: on in a down clue says the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: a sewing needle has an eye for the thread
SS, steamship, is a boat

explanation.surface: Someone keeping an eye on a boat they bought as an indulgence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One with eye' looks like a person, but is a needle.
explanation.definitionFit: A luxury is by nature unnecessary, something not needed.

clue.text: Unshaven artist hosts posh opening of exhibition

indicators.note: hosts says the artist holds the next letter inside

parts.note: Damien Hirst is a British artist
U is the label for upper-class, posh usage

indicators.note: opening takes the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A scruffy, unshaved artist hosts a smart gallery opening.
explanation.walkthrough: Damien Hirst is the British artist of the pickled shark; 'hosts' puts U inside his name.
explanation.definitionFit: Hirsute means hairy, so a face that has not been shaved.

clue.text: Cathedral city's ambassador welcomed by rectors all over the place

indicators.note: welcomed by says the ambassador is taken in by the clergymen
all over the place means scattered, so the clergymen's letters are rearranged

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is how an ambassador is styled

explanation.surface: A cathedral city's envoy is received by clergy scattered everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all over the place' is the anagram signal; 'welcomed by' says the envoy sits inside the scrambled clergy, and 'ambassador' gives His Excellency's initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Rochester in Kent has one of England's oldest cathedrals.

clue.text: Elders, perhaps, about to split gang up

indicators.note: to split means to break apart, so this goes into the middle
up in a down clue reads the gang backwards

parts.note: a set is a group of people, a gang
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Church elders try to break up a gang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elders' tempts as senior people, but it is a tree; 'up' gives TES and 'to split' puts RE inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Elder is a shrub or small tree, so elders are examples of trees.

clue.text: State of increased activity finished Verdi off

parts.note: something finished is over

indicators.note: off means gone bad or out of order, so the composer's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone in a frenzy of energy has polished off the whole of Verdi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' reads as finishing the composer, but it is the anagram signal, and 'finished' supplies the first half.
explanation.definitionFit: Going into overdrive means working at a frantic, heightened pace.

clue.text: Scout told to disable base

indicators.note: told signals that the word is spoken, giving its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: to wreck a machine is to disable it by destroying it
e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: A boy scout is instructed to put the base camp out of action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'told' gives the sound of WRECK, written RECC; E is the mathematical base of natural logarithms.
explanation.definitionFit: A recce is a reconnaissance, and to recce is to scout an area ahead.

clue.text: Misguided 22 half-heartedly containing strong attack die

indicators.note: containing says the rearranged letters hold the attack inside them
misguided means led astray, so the remaining letters are rearranged
the city's heart is its two central letters, and losing half of that heart removes one of them

parts.note: 22 refers to the solution of 22-down, the American city
a KO is a knockout, a blow strong enough to floor someone

explanation.surface: A misguided strike on 22, carried out half-heartedly, fails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-heartedly' loses one of the two central letters of the city; 'Misguided' rearranges the rest as CONUT, and 'containing' wraps that round the knockout.
explanation.definitionFit: Conk out is informal for a machine or person failing completely, or dying.

clue.text: Kudos being related to comedian

definitions.meaning: kudos means honour and acclaim, as won by a victor's wreath
belonging to Stan Laurel, the thin half of the comedy double act Laurel and Hardy

explanation.surface: Fame comes from being kin to a famous comic.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense reads the answer as a possessive, LAUREL'S, as in belonging to Stan Laurel.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurels are honours, from the bay wreath awarded to victors in ancient Greece.

clue.text: Distinguished circles graduate rejected for mates, maybe

indicators.note: circles means surrounds, so the first word goes around the second

parts.note: a thing distinguished has been seen or made out

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the degree is read backwards

parts.note: an MA, a Master of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: Eminent social circles turn down a graduate in favour of friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mates' are not friends but ship's officers, who are among the sailors; 'circles' and 'rejected' do the work.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's mate is one example of a sailor, hence the 'maybe'.

clue.text: Quietly leaving restless Persian cat to settle

indicators.note: restless means unable to keep still, so the cat's letters move about
leaving says the quiet letter departs from the cat's

parts.note: the words Persian cat supply the letters to rearrange
p, piano, is the music term for quietly

explanation.surface: A Persian cat sneaks away restlessly before curling up to sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' drops P from PERSIAN CAT and 'restless' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle a question is to determine it, or ascertain the answer.

clue.text: Put a note in garment to be returned

indicators.note: in places the note inside the turned garment
returned means sent back, so the garment is read backwards

parts.note: a dress is a garment
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Instructions to slip a note into a garment before sending it back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be returned' makes SSERD, and 'in' places the sol-fa note inside it; 'Put' means stated, as in putting a case.
explanation.definitionFit: To put a case or argument is to state it, which is to assert it.

clue.text: Some distance northwards, husky announced as load-bearer

indicators.note: northwards in a down clue reads the distance upwards, backwards

parts.note: a yard is a short distance

indicators.note: announced says the word is spoken, giving its sound

parts.note: a husky voice is hoarse

explanation.surface: A sled dog travels some way north, hauling cargo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'husky' looks like the sled dog, but is the hoarse voice; 'northwards' gives DRAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A dray horse pulls a heavy cart, a beast of burden.

clue.text: Expert raised underside of calico steed's muzzle

parts.note: a gun is slang for an expert, as in top gun

indicators.note: raised says the bottom letter of the down entry is lifted higher in the horse

parts.note: a pinto is a piebald, calico-patterned horse

explanation.surface: An expert lifts a piebald horse's hoof to inspect its muzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised underside of' moves the last O of PINTO up to second place, making POINT.
explanation.definitionFit: Being held at gunpoint means facing a gun's muzzle.

clue.text: A breeze over the pond is nothing very amiss

parts.note: in cricket a duck is a score of nothing
so means very, as in so good
something up is wrong, as in what's up?

explanation.surface: A light wind blowing across a duck pond causes no disturbance at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over the pond' means in America, across the Atlantic; there duck soup is something easy. 'Pond' tempts toward ducks, which turns out half right.
explanation.definitionFit: American slang calls an easy task duck soup, just as Britons call it a breeze.

clue.text: Having IT installed, very good for Texan poet

indicators.note: installed says the computing letters go inside

parts.note: swell is American slang for very good

explanation.surface: A Texan poet is pleased to have new computers fitted.
explanation.walkthrough: Edith Sitwell was an English poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Edith Sitwell was a celebrated English modernist poet.

clue.text: Masonry crumbles over abandoned ancient place

indicators.note: masonry that crumbles falls apart, so its letters are rearranged once one is gone
abandoned says the over is left out of the rubble

parts.note: the word masonry supplies the letters to rearrange
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Stonework falls apart above a deserted ancient site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' drops O from MASONRY and 'crumbles' rearranges the rest. Smyrna was an ancient Greek city, now Izmir in Turkey.
explanation.definitionFit: Smyrna was a city of the ancient world on the Aegean coast.

clue.text: Having a zero taken from $1,000,000,000 is crushing

indicators.note: taken from says the zero is removed

parts.note: a million grand, G being a grand or thousand dollars
O is a zero

explanation.surface: Losing a nought from a billion dollars is a crushing blow.
explanation.walkthrough: A billion dollars is a million thousands, MILLION G, G being slang for a grand; 'taken from' removes an O.
explanation.definitionFit: Milling grain means grinding or crushing it.

clue.text: Numbers diminished coming from South American city

indicators.note: coming from the south in a down clue means reading upwards, backwards

parts.note: something cut has been diminished

explanation.surface: Reduced numbers coming from a South American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South American' looks like one phrase, but 'South' belongs to the wordplay and the city is in Arizona.
explanation.definitionFit: Tucson is a city in Arizona in the United States.

clue.text: Practical surface's better on run

indicators.note: on says the second piece comes after the first

parts.note: a machine that runs works
to better a rival is to top them

explanation.surface: A useful surface makes a good place to put your running gear.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', a link between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen worktop is a flat surface for practical tasks like chopping.

clue.text: Ones playing together with reptiles

parts.note: asps are venomous snakes, reptiles

explanation.surface: Children playing alongside snakes.
explanation.walkthrough: Wasps is an English rugby union club, a team.
explanation.definitionFit: Wasps is a rugby club, a team of players who play together.

clue.text: Release Frenchman's one son in field hospital

parts.note: un is French for one

indicators.note: in places the son within the field and hospital

parts.note: a lea is a meadow or field
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's boy is discharged from a field hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts S between LEA and H.
explanation.definitionFit: To unleash something is to set it free, or release it.

clue.text: Grief from back after carrying monarch once

indicators.note: carrying says the time word holds the monarch inside

parts.note: ago means back in time, as in years back
GR, Georgius Rex, was the royal cipher of the old King Georges

explanation.surface: Grief arrives after a king of old is carried away.
explanation.walkthrough: GR is the royal cipher of past King Georges.
explanation.definitionFit: Grief and aggro are both informal British words for hassle and aggression.

clue.text: Drink well, consume in The Queen Vic

parts.note: so and well both open a remark, as in so, what now?

indicators.note: the Queen Vic is the pub in the London soap EastEnders, where Cockney speech drops the opening aitch

parts.note: to have a meal is to consume it

explanation.surface: A soap character is invited to sup a pint in the Queen Vic.
explanation.walkthrough: The Queen Vic is the pub in EastEnders, a British TV soap set in Cockney London, where HAVE is said 'AVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Soave is a dry white Italian wine, so a drink.

clue.text: Swerving ball from key footballer

parts.note: Ins is the Insert key on a keyboard
a winger plays on the flank in football

explanation.surface: A curling shot comes from a crucial player on the wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key' is not crucial but the Insert key.
explanation.definitionFit: An inswinger is a cricket or football delivery that curves in towards its target.

clue.text: One to divulge information twice

parts.note: to sing is slang for telling the police what you know
twice says the same idea is given a second time, in the phrase let on, meaning reveal a secret

explanation.surface: A single person is asked to tell what they know two times over.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay defines 'divulge information' twice, in two different ways: SING, then LET ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A singleton is a single thing, one on its own rather than part of a pair.

clue.text: Range on header from Geoff Hurst

indicators.note: on says the roaming word follows the letter
a header is the top piece, so this takes the opening letter of the name

parts.note: to range is to roam, or rove

explanation.surface: Geoff Hurst, England's 1966 World Cup hat-trick hero, scores with a header from range.
explanation.walkthrough: Geoff Hurst scored a hat-trick in the 1966 World Cup final; 'Hurst' is really a word for a wooded hill.
explanation.definitionFit: Hurst is an old word for a wood or copse, like a grove.
